youtube.title: Rust Day 7: bool, char & What Is 255 + 1? 🦀 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Rust Day 7: bool, char and integer overflow, explained line by line. What really happens when a u8 hits 255 + 1?

📌 In this short:
✅ bool is true or false; char uses single quotes, holds any Unicode character and is 4 bytes
✅ 255 + 1 on a u8: Rust refuses to compile it; at runtime debug builds panic and release builds wrap
✅ Choose the behaviour: checked_add (None), wrapping_add (0), saturating_add (255)

💻 Code from the video:
fn main() {
    let x: u8 = 255;
    let a = x.checked_add(1);    // None
    let b = x.wrapping_add(1);   // 0
    let c = x.saturating_add(1); // 255
    println!("{a:?} {b} {c}");
}

📖 Learn more: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-02-data-types.html

scenes.heading: Caught at compile time
scenes.caption: this would overflow
scenes.say: Rust refuses to compile it: this arithmetic operation will overflow. When it can't spot it early, a debug build panics at runtime, and a release build wraps around to zero.
